en: Mayon Volcano's perfect cone forms because repeated eruptions deposit alternating layers of cooled lava and volcanic ash.
The Pasig River temporarily flows backward during high tide because seawater from Manila Bay pushes against the current.
The Habagat monsoon brings heavy rains to western Luzon because it carries abundant moisture evaporated from the West Philippine Sea.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills turn brown during the dry season because the intense heat dries the grass covering the mounds.
Palawan's mangrove forests protect coastlines from storm surges because their dense, tangled root systems absorb crashing ocean waves.
Lake Taal is a lake inside a volcano because an ancient eruption collapsed the ground into a water-filled crater.
Mount Pulag's famous sea of clouds forms when cold mountain air condenses the warm, moist air rising from below.
Puerto Princesa's Underground River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the soluble limestone bedrock over millions of years.
Tubbataha's coral reefs grow because tiny coral polyps continuously secrete calcium carbonate to build hard, accumulating skeletal structures.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent soil erosion on steep mountains because carved stone walls and flooded paddies hold the dirt.
The Kuroshio Current warms the eastern coast of Luzon because it transports warm tropical water northward from the Pacific.
The Valley Fault System triggers earthquakes because sliding tectonic plates suddenly release massive amounts of built-up underground stress.
